en: designer; planner (of a structure or system)

examples.en: The designer of this bridge is a foreigner.
The designer revised the drawing again.

examples.ko: 건물 설계자를 직접 만나 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to meet the building's designer in person.

examples.ko: 그는 이 도시를 만든 설계자로 불려요.
examples.en: He is called the designer who created this city.
The designer's ideas show all over the building.
I had a meeting with the program's designer.

explain: 건물, 다리, 기계, 시스템의 구조를 계획하는 사람이에요. 옷이나 포스터를 꾸미는 사람은 '디자이너'라고 하고, 설계자는 구조와 계획 쪽에 써요. 건축 쪽에서는 '건축가'라고도 해요.
explain_en: A 설계자 plans the structure of buildings, bridges, machines or systems. Someone who styles clothes or posters is a 디자이너. In architecture you will also hear 건축가.

examples.ko: 그는 고전부터 현대 소설까지 다 섭렵했어요.
examples.en: He has read everything from the classics to modern novels.

examples.ko: 방학 동안 이 분야의 책을 모두 섭렵하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work through all the books in this field during the vacation.
He is a chef who has mastered the cuisines of many countries.

examples.ko: 한 번에 다 섭렵하려고 하면 금방 지쳐요.
examples.en: If you try to cover everything at once, you get tired quickly.

examples.ko: 그 감독의 영화를 섭렵해 보니 스타일이 보였어요.
examples.en: After going through that director's films, I could see his style.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 발라드와 록을 두루 섭렵했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that singer has covered both ballads and rock thoroughly.

explain: 책, 장르, 작품처럼 여러 개를 두루 접해서 많이 안다는 느낌으로 써요. 하나만 깊이 공부할 때는 '파고들다'가 더 어울리고, '섭렵하다'는 폭넓게 훑는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used for going through many things such as books, genres or works and coming to know a lot of them. For studying just one thing deeply, '파고들다' fits better, while '섭렵하다' has a feel of covering a wide range.

en: to belong to; to be affiliated

examples.en: I belong to the sales team.
Which team did that player belong to?
It's a research institute affiliated with a university.
Where are you affiliated now?
If you belong to a company, you get insurance.
I'm anxious because I don't belong to anywhere yet.

explain: '~에 소속하다'는 조직에 속해 있다는 뜻인데, 말할 때는 '~에 속해 있다'나 '~ 소속이다'를 더 많이 써요. 소개할 때도 '○○ 소속이에요'처럼 명사로 써요. 소속하다는 글이나 공식적인 말에 가까워요.
explain_en: The pattern is ~에 소속하다, but in speech people more often say ~에 속해 있다 or ~ 소속이다. When introducing yourself you use the noun, like '○○ 소속이에요'. The verb itself sounds written or official.

dis.h: active form, rarer; belong to organization

examples.ko: 그 마을에는 도자기를 만드는 수공업자가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many craftsmen who make pottery in that village.

examples.ko: 수공업자들은 직접 손으로 물건을 만들어 팔았어요.
examples.en: The craftsmen made things by hand and sold them.
Bags made by craftsmen are known for being sturdy.
Craftsmen in the old days worked while helping each other.
My father is a craftsman who runs a small shop.
As machines appeared, the craftsmen's work decreased.

explain: '장인'은 솜씨가 뛰어난 사람을 높여 부르는 말이고, '수공업자'는 손으로 물건을 만들어 먹고사는 사람을 가리키는 중립적인 말이에요. 역사나 경제 설명에서 주로 나와요.
explain_en: '장인' is a respectful word for a person of outstanding skill, while '수공업자' is a neutral word for someone who makes a living by making things by hand. It mostly appears in history and economics explanations.

examples.en: I want to study veterinary science at university.

examples.ko: 수의학과에 들어가려면 점수가 아주 높아야 해요.
examples.en: You need very high scores to get into the veterinary department.
A friend who majored in veterinary science opened an animal hospital.
I hear that in veterinary science you learn about cows and horses too.
Veterinary science is popular these days because there are more pets.

examples.ko: 형은 수의학 박사 과정에 다니고 있어요.
examples.en: My older brother is in a doctoral program in veterinary science.

explain: 동물의 병을 보는 사람은 '수의사'라고 하고, 사람의 병을 다루는 공부는 '의학'이라고 해요. 대학에서는 '수의학과'나 '수의과대학'이라는 이름을 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: A person who treats animal illnesses is called a '수의사' (veterinarian), while the study of human illness is '의학' (medicine). At universities you will see the names '수의학과' or '수의과대학'.

examples.en: I carry out important work at the company.
The team carried out the mission safely.
I want to perform my role well.
There is not enough time to carry out the assignment.
The result differs depending on who carries it out.
We carried it out as planned and succeeded.

explain: '하다'보다 딱딱하고, 맡은 임무나 과제를 끝까지 해낸다는 느낌이에요. '수행평가'는 학교에서 수업 중 과제를 평가하는 말이에요. 일, 임무, 역할, 과제와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than the plain verb for doing, with a sense of carrying an assigned task through. A related school word names in-class performance assessment. It pairs well with work, mission, role and assignment.

dis.h: carry out a task or duty

p.n: 실시하다 stresses putting a planned survey into effect.

examples.en: A skilled technician fixed the machine right away.

examples.ko: 일을 오래 하면 손이 숙련돼서 훨씬 빨라져요.
examples.en: If you work for a long time, your hands become practiced and much faster.
I'm not proficient yet, so I make a lot of mistakes.

examples.ko: 이 일에 숙련되기까지 보통 몇 년이 걸려요.
examples.en: It usually takes a few years to become proficient at this job.

examples.ko: 그 요리사는 칼질이 정말 숙련돼 보여요.
examples.en: That chef's knife work looks really practiced.
After practicing for a long time, I'm now quite proficient.

explain: '숙련된 기술자', '숙련된 솜씨'처럼 사람이나 솜씨를 꾸미는 말로 많이 써요. '능숙하다'는 익숙하고 솜씨가 좋다는 느낌이고, '숙련되다'는 연습과 경험으로 그렇게 된 과정이 느껴져요. 반대말은 '미숙하다'예요.
explain_en: It is often used to describe people or skills, as in '숙련된 기술자' or '숙련된 솜씨'. '능숙하다' simply says someone is smooth and good at something, while '숙련되다' carries the sense of having become so through practice and experience. The opposite is '미숙하다'.

examples.en: This school trains excellent cooks.

examples.ko: 정부가 젊은 과학자를 양성하려고 지원금을 줬어요.
examples.en: The government gave funding to nurture young scientists.
I want to attend a university that trains teachers.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 신입 사원을 전문가로 양성했어요.
examples.en: Our company trained its new employees to become experts.

examples.ko: 축구 선수를 양성할 학원이 우리 동네에 생겼어요.
examples.en: An academy to train soccer players opened in our neighborhood.
It takes a long time to develop talented people.

explain: '가르치다'는 지식을 알려 주는 것이고, '양성하다'는 어떤 일을 할 사람으로 키워 내는 것이에요. 목적어는 사람이고 '인재', '전문가', '선수'와 자주 같이 써요. 집에서 아이를 키울 때는 '키우다'를 써요.
explain_en: '가르치다' means to teach knowledge, while '양성하다' means to raise people into those who can do a certain job. The object is a person, often '인재' (talent), '전문가' (expert), or '선수' (athlete). For raising a child at home, use '키우다'.

p.n: 양성 means producing professionals; 훈련시키다 means drilling skills.

examples.en: He served as minister twice.
This is a person who served as a professor and department chair.
The person who long served as chairman stepped down.
After holding a number of posts, he retired.

examples.ko: 시장을 역임할 때 도로를 많이 만들었어요.
examples.en: While serving as mayor, he built many roads.
I hear he has a lot of experience from having served as CEO.

explain: 회사나 정부에서 높은 직책을 차례로 맡았다는 뜻이라 소개 글이나 뉴스에서 써요. 지금 하는 일에는 쓰지 않고 이미 지난 경력에 써요. 일상 말로는 '~을 했어요', '~로 일했어요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means someone took on high positions one after another in a company or government, so it appears in profiles and the news. It is used for past career history, not for the job someone is doing now. In everyday speech people say '~을 했어요' or '~로 일했어요'.

examples.en: My father is a welder who works at a shipyard.
The welder joins steel plates, sparks flying.
You need a certificate to become a welder.
My uncle is a welder with twenty years of experience.

examples.ko: 용접공은 보호 안경을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: Welders must wear protective goggles.

examples.ko: 현장에서 용접공 두 명이 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: Two welders are working at the site.

explain: 직업을 말할 때는 '용접공이에요'라고도 하고 '용접 일을 해요'라고도 해요. 기술 직업 이름에 붙는 '-공'은 기술자를 나타내요. 현장 이야기나 구인 공고에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: To say the job you can say '용접공이에요' or '용접 일을 해요'. The '-공' ending marks a skilled worker. You often see it in talk about work sites and in job ads.

examples.en: The teacher led the students to the museum.
A travel agency staff member is leading the tourists.

examples.ko: 제가 아이들을 인솔할 테니 걱정 마세요.
examples.en: I'll take charge of the children, so don't worry.
Leading a group is harder than you'd think.

examples.ko: 제가 인솔한 학생은 모두 열 명이에요.
examples.en: The students I led number ten in all.

examples.ko: 소풍 때 반 아이들을 인솔하며 길을 건넜어요.
examples.en: On the picnic, I crossed the road leading the class.

explain: '데리고 가다'와 달리 선생님, 가이드처럼 단체를 책임지고 이끌 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '데리고 가요'가 더 자연스럽고, 이끄는 사람은 '인솔자'라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '데리고 가다', it is used when someone such as a teacher or guide takes responsibility for leading a group. In casual talk '데리고 가요' sounds more natural, and the person in charge is called '인솔자'.

dis.h: lead a group on a trip

p.n: 인솔 is formal and means accompanying a group; 이끌다 is general leading.

en: one's own views; good grasp of something

examples.en: He really knows his way around cooking.
My father is quite an expert at baduk.

examples.ko: 커피에 일가견이 있는 친구에게 추천을 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I asked a friend who knows a lot about coffee for a recommendation.

examples.ko: 언니는 옷 고르는 데 일가견이 있어요.
examples.en: My older sister has a real eye for picking out clothes.

examples.ko: 이 분야에 일가견을 가진 전문가를 만났어요.
examples.en: I met an expert with deep insight into this field.

examples.ko: 여행 계획 짜는 일에는 제가 일가견이 있어요.
examples.en: When it comes to planning trips, I have a knack for it.

explain: '잘하다'나 '잘 알다'보다 자기만의 안목과 실력이 인정될 만하다는 느낌이에요. 거의 '~에 일가견이 있다' 꼴로 쓰고, 자기 자신에게 쓰면 조금 으스대는 느낌일 수 있어요.

phrases.en: be very knowledgeable about; have a good eye for
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 분야를 오래 접해서 자기만의 안목이 있다는 뜻으로, '일가견'만 따로는 잘 안 쓰고 이 꼴로 굳어 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means someone has a well-developed eye for a field after long experience. '일가견' is rarely used alone and is fixed in this phrase.
phrases.en_equiv: know a thing or two about

explain_en: Compared with '잘하다' or '잘 알다', it suggests you have your own discerning eye and skill that others would recognize. It is almost always used as '~에 일가견이 있다', and using it about yourself can sound a little boastful.

examples.ko: 일신상의 사정으로 이번 달까지만 일할 거예요.
examples.en: For personal reasons, I will only work until the end of this month.

examples.ko: 일신상 문제 때문에 오늘 모임에 못 가요.
examples.en: I can't go to today's meeting because of a personal matter.
Something difficult came up in my personal life, so I took a leave of absence.

examples.ko: 일신상에 문제가 있어서 이번 대회는 쉬기로 했어요.
examples.en: Because of a personal problem, I decided to sit out this competition.
I only wrote 'personal reasons' on my resignation letter.

examples.ko: 일신상 이유라고 하면 보통 더 묻지 않아요.
examples.en: When someone says it's for personal reasons, people usually don't ask more.

explain: '개인적인'을 격식 있게 말하는 표현으로, 회사나 서류에서 '일신상의 이유/사유/사정'이라고 많이 써요. 자세한 이유를 말하고 싶지 않을 때도 쓰지요. 친구와 말할 때는 '개인적인 일'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a formal way of saying 'personal', commonly seen at work and in documents as '일신상의 이유/사유/사정'. It is also used when you don't want to give the details. With friends you would say '개인적인 일'.

examples.ko: 올해 재수생이 된 형이 학원에 다녀요.
examples.en: My older brother, who became a retaker this year, goes to a cram school.

examples.ko: 재수생은 공부 시간 관리가 정말 중요해요.
examples.en: For retakers, managing study time is really important.

examples.ko: 재수생으로 지내는 동안 친구들과 연락이 뜸해졌어요.
examples.en: While I was a retaker, I kept in touch with my friends less.

examples.ko: 내 사촌은 작년에 재수생 생활을 하고 올해 합격했어요.
examples.en: My cousin lived as a retaker last year and passed this year.

examples.ko: 재수생들을 위한 상담 프로그램이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new counseling program for retakers has been created.

examples.ko: 재수생인데도 매일 웃으며 공부하는 친구가 대단해요.
examples.en: My friend studies with a smile every day even as a retaker, which is impressive.

explain: 대학 입시에서 한 번 떨어지거나 결과에 만족하지 못해 다시 준비하는 사람이에요. 줄여서 '재수'라고 하고, '재수하다'는 동사예요. 한 번 더 하면 '삼수생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who fails or is unsatisfied with a university entrance exam and prepares again. It is shortened to '재수', and '재수하다' is the verb. Someone who does it one more time is called a '삼수생'.

en: to hold a post; to be employed (formal)

examples.ko: 저는 이 회사에 십 년째 재직하고 있어요.
examples.en: I have been employed at this company for ten years.
He is a teacher who once worked at our school.
I learned a lot while I was employed there.

examples.ko: 재직할 때 만난 사람들과 아직 연락해요.
examples.en: I still keep in touch with the people I met while working there.
Before joining the university, I worked at a research institute.
Working here, I met good people.

explain: 어떤 직장에 속해서 일하고 있을 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. '일하다'는 어디서나 쓰지만 '재직하다'는 서류나 소개에서 '재직 증명서', '재직 중'처럼 써요. 직장을 그만두면 '퇴직하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a formal word for being employed by an organization. '일하다' works everywhere, but '재직하다' appears in documents and introductions, as in '재직 증명서' (employment certificate) and '재직 중' (currently employed). When you leave the job, it becomes '퇴직하다'.

dis.h: formal: hold a post at an organization

p.s: 아버지는 이 회사에 십 년째 재직하고 있다.
p.o: 아버지는 이 회사에 십 년째 근무하고 있다.
p.n: 재직하다 stresses being employed in a position and is formal and written. 근무하다 stresses the actual working.

examples.en: I'm currently enrolled in university.
My younger sibling is enrolled in high school.
I received a scholarship while I was enrolled.

examples.ko: 그는 대학교에 재학할 때 유학을 다녀왔어요.
examples.en: He went abroad to study while he was in university.

examples.ko: 이 학교에 재학 중인 학생은 도서관을 무료로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Students currently enrolled at this school can use the library for free.

examples.ko: 재학생이 아니면 학생 할인을 못 받아요.
examples.en: If you aren't a current student, you can't get the student discount.

explain: 학교에 다니고 있는 상태를 서류나 소개에서 말할 때 써요. 일상 말로는 '다니다'가 자연스러워요. '재학생', '재학 중', '재학 증명서'로 자주 나오고, 졸업했으면 '졸업생', 쉬고 있으면 '휴학 중'이에요.
explain_en: Use it for the state of attending school in documents and introductions. In everyday speech 다니다 sounds more natural. It appears as '재학생', '재학 중', and '재학 증명서'; graduates are 졸업생 and those on leave are '휴학 중'.

en: to move frequently; to move; to hop about

examples.ko: 그는 취직이 안 돼서 아르바이트를 전전했어요.
examples.en: He couldn't get a regular job and drifted from one part-time job to another.

examples.ko: 집값이 올라서 이 동네 저 동네를 전전하며 살았어요.
examples.en: House prices went up, so I lived moving from neighborhood to neighborhood.

examples.ko: 친구 집을 전전하는 생활도 이제 끝났어요.
examples.en: The life of hopping from one friend's house to another is over now.

examples.ko: 일자리를 전전하다 보니 한 곳에서 오래 일해 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: Because I kept hopping between jobs, I've never worked long in one place.
Even after going from hospital to hospital, I couldn't find the cause.
I still remember the days of moving from one rented room to another.

explain: 한곳에 머물지 못하고 여기저기 옮겨 다닌다는 뜻이고, 힘든 상황이라는 느낌이 있어요. '직장을 전전하다', '병원을 전전하다'처럼 목적어를 꼭 같이 써요. 일상에서는 '옮겨 다니다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It means being unable to stay in one place and moving around, and it carries a feel of hard circumstances. It is always used with an object, as in '직장을 전전하다' or '병원을 전전하다'. In daily talk people also say '옮겨 다니다'.

examples.en: The gardener is trimming the rose bushes.
My father worked as a gardener for a long time.

examples.ko: 우리 집 정원은 정원사가 관리해 줘요.
examples.en: A gardener looks after our house's garden.
Thanks to the gardener, the yard became tidy.
I want to become a gardener someday.

examples.ko: 공원 정원사는 아침마다 꽃에 물을 줘요.
examples.en: The park gardener waters the flowers every morning.

explain: '요리사', '미용사'처럼 '사'가 붙은 직업 이름이에요. 집에서 취미로 가꾸는 사람은 보통 '정원사'라고 하지 않고 '정원을 가꾸다'라고 말해요. 일로 하는 사람이라는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: Like '요리사' and '미용사', the '사' ending marks a profession. Someone who gardens at home as a hobby is not usually called a '정원사'; people say '정원을 가꾸다' instead. The word carries a sense of doing it as a job.

examples.en: Which production company made this movie?
The production company announced a new drama.
My dream is to work at a big production company.
I emailed the game production company with a question.
The production company and the broadcaster signed a contract.

examples.ko: 제작사 이름은 영화가 끝날 때 나와요.
examples.en: The production company's name appears when the movie ends.

explain: 영화·드라마·음악·게임을 실제로 만드는 회사를 말해요. 방송을 내보내는 곳은 '방송사', 물건을 만드는 회사는 보통 '제조사'라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: The company that actually makes a film, drama, music, or game. The one that airs it is the '방송사' (broadcaster), and a company that manufactures goods is usually a '제조사'.

en: to be devoted; to dedicate oneself

examples.en: I worked in the field of education for a long time.
My father works in agriculture.

examples.ko: 이 일에 종사하는 사람이 점점 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of people working in this job is shrinking.
I went to university because I wanted to work in the medical field.
It's a job that requires a license to work in.

examples.ko: 서비스업에 종사한 지 십 년이 되었어요.
examples.en: It's been ten years since I started working in the service industry.

explain: '일하다'는 어디서나 쓰지만 종사하다는 분야나 업종에 써요. '교육에 종사하다'처럼 조사 '에'를 붙이고, 회사 이름 앞에는 쓰지 않아요. 직업을 소개하는 자리나 서류에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: 일하다 works anywhere, but 종사하다 is for a field or industry. It takes the particle 에, as in '교육에 종사하다', and is not used with a company name. You often see it when introducing a career or on forms.

en: to take the lead; to take the initiative

examples.en: Minsu leads the meeting.
Our team took the lead on this event.
It's good when children take the lead in their own study.

examples.ko: 새로운 사업을 주도할 사람을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We're looking for someone to lead the new business.
The one who drives the conversation is always my older sister.
He is leading the reform.

explain: '주도하다'는 앞장서서 이끌고 일이 가는 방향을 잡을 때 써요. '이끌다'보다 딱딱해서 회의, 사업, 대화, 개혁 같은 말과 자주 나와요. '학습을 주도하다'처럼 스스로 하는 모습에도 써요.
explain_en: 주도하다 means to take the front and set the direction of something. It is more formal than 이끌다 and often goes with meetings, business, conversation and reform. It also fits self-directed things like '학습을 주도하다' (to lead one's own study).

p.n: 리드하다 is a casual loanword for guiding the flow; 주도하다 means taking charge.

examples.en: The teacher guides the students' presentations.
I coached the juniors in the club.
The teacher who coaches exercise has come.
I'm grateful to the professor who advises my thesis.
You need patience when guiding children.
I have experience guiding students for a long time.

explain: 가르치고 이끄는 일이에요. '가르치다'는 지식을 전하는 것이고, '지도하다'는 방향을 잡아 주고 도와주는 느낌이 강해요. 명사 '지도'는 'map'과 소리가 같아서 문맥으로 구별해야 해요.
explain_en: It means teaching and leading. The plain verb for 'teach' passes on knowledge, while this one stresses setting a direction and helping along. The noun form sounds the same as the word for a map, so context tells them apart.

dis.h: teach or coach, like a teacher

p.n: Becomes showing the student around or giving information, not coaching.

examples.en: I'm studying geography at university.

examples.ko: 지리학 수업에서 지도 읽는 법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In geography class, we learned how to read maps.
My older brother respects his geography professor.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에 지리학 수업을 두 개 들어요.
examples.en: I'm taking two geography classes this semester.
Geographers made a new map.
Geography has human geography and physical geography.

explain: 학교 과목은 '지리'이고, 대학에서 공부하는 학문은 '지리학'이에요. '지리학과', '지리학자'처럼 뒤에 붙는 말이 많아요. 인문지리와 자연지리로 크게 나눠요.
explain_en: The school subject is 지리, while the university field is 지리학. Common extensions are 지리학과 (department) and 지리학자 (geographer). It splits mainly into human geography and physical geography.

en: to be recruited; to be hired

examples.en: I was hired by a big company this year.
I did well in the interview and was hired right away.
New employees are usually hired in March.
The person who was hired starts work next week.
Can I be hired even without experience?
It's rare to be hired just by submitting documents.

explain: '뽑히다'는 말할 때 쓰는 편한 표현이고, '채용되다'는 공식적인 느낌이에요. 회사가 사람을 쓸 때 '채용하다'나 '뽑다'를 쓰고, 합격은 '붙다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '뽑히다' is the casual spoken form; '채용되다' sounds more official. A company says '채용하다' or '뽑다', and passing is also called '붙다'.

p.n: 모집되다 doesn't fit a person getting hired; it is for the call for applicants.

examples.en: I think being a teacher is my true calling.

examples.ko: 그는 환자를 돌보는 일을 천직으로 여겨요.
examples.en: He regards caring for patients as his calling.

examples.ko: 이 일이 천직인지 아직 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I'm still not sure whether this job is my calling.

examples.ko: 할머니는 평생 농사를 천직으로 알고 사셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother lived her whole life taking farming as her calling.
You work happily, like someone who has found their calling.

examples.ko: 요리사가 천직이라서 하루 종일 일해도 힘들지 않아요.
examples.en: Being a chef is my calling, so I'm not tired even after working all day.

explain: '직업'과 달리 나에게 딱 맞는 평생 할 일이라는 애정이 담겨 있어요. '천직으로 여기다', '천직으로 삼다', '천직이다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '직업' (job), it carries affection, meaning work that fits you perfectly and that you would do for life. It is used as '천직으로 여기다', '천직으로 삼다' or '천직이다'.

en: to apply for; to file an application for

examples.en: We filed the new technology as a patent.
I'm going to file the company name as a trademark.
It's safer to file this idea first.
I heard he filed applications for as many as three inventions.
Sir, when did you file for that design?
After you file, you have to wait for the examination.

explain: '특허를 출원하다', '상표를 출원하다'처럼 권리를 신청할 때 써요. 입학이나 취업은 '출원'이 아니라 '지원하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used for applying for rights, as in '특허를 출원하다' and '상표를 출원하다'. For admissions or jobs, use '지원하다' instead, not '출원하다'.

examples.en: The uncle got his nephew a job at his company.

examples.ko: 부모님은 아들을 빨리 취직시키고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The parents want to get their son a job quickly.

examples.ko: 선배가 저를 아는 회사에 취직시켜 줬어요.
examples.en: A senior got me a job at a company he knows.
The father tried hard to get his daughter a job at a bank.
I thanked the boss who gave my friend a job.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 취직시킬 방법이 없어서 고민이에요.
examples.en: I am worried because there is no way to get that person a job.

explain: 'A가 B를 회사에 취직시키다'처럼 일하게 해 주는 사람과 일자리를 얻는 사람이 따로 있어요. 내가 일자리를 얻는 건 '취직하다'를 써요.
explain_en: In 'A가 B를 회사에 취직시키다', the person who arranges the job and the person who gets it are different. When you get a job yourself, use '취직하다'.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 코미디언이 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I wanted to be a comedian since I was little.
That comedian makes people laugh with just his expression.
I saw a famous comedian on TV yesterday.

examples.ko: 코미디언 친구가 생일 파티에서 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: My comedian friend sang a song at the birthday party.
If you talk like a comedian, the mood loosens up quickly.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 코미디언 같은 학생이 한 명 있어요.
examples.en: There is one student in our class who is like a comedian.

explain: 방송에서는 '개그맨', '개그우먼'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요. 코미디언은 성별과 상관없이 쓸 수 있어서 소개할 때 안전한 말이에요. 재미있는 친구에게는 보통 '웃긴 사람'이라고 해요.
explain_en: On Korean TV people often say 개그맨 and 개그우먼. 코미디언 works for any gender, so it is a safe word when you introduce someone. For a funny friend, people usually just say 웃긴 사람.

examples.en: My uncle works as a programmer at a big company.
The programmer made a new app.
I have dreamed of being a programmer since I was young.
Programmers often work at night.
The programmer's desk is full of coffee.
The programmer and the designer hold a meeting together.

explain: 회사에서는 '개발자'라는 말도 자주 써요. 두 말을 거의 같은 사람에게 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 직업을 말할 때는 '프로그래머로 일하다'처럼 '로'를 붙여요.
explain_en: Companies also use the word '개발자' (developer), and the two often refer to the same people. When naming the job, add '로', as in '프로그래머로 일하다'.

examples.en: The principal greeted the students at the graduation ceremony.
I wrote a letter addressed to the principal.

examples.ko: 우리 학교장은 아침마다 정문에서 학생들을 맞아요.
examples.en: Our principal greets students at the front gate every morning.

examples.ko: 학교장의 허락을 받아야 행사를 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can hold the event only with the principal's permission.
There was a time to introduce the new principal.

examples.ko: 학교장 추천서가 있어야 지원할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can apply only with a letter of recommendation from the principal.

explain: 말할 때는 '교장 선생님'이라고 부르고, '학교장'은 공문, 서류, 뉴스에서 주로 써요. '학교장 추천', '학교장 허가'처럼 제도 이름에 많이 나와요. 학교 안에서 직접 부를 때는 꼭 '교장 선생님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In speech people say '교장 선생님'; '학교장' is mostly for official letters, documents, and news. It often appears in system names like '학교장 추천' and '학교장 허가'. At school, address the person as '교장 선생님'.

examples.en: I studied Korean in my undergraduate program.

examples.ko: 학부 때는 친구들과 동아리 활동을 많이 했어요.
examples.en: In my undergraduate years, I did a lot of club activities with friends.

examples.ko: 학부를 졸업한 뒤에 대학원에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: After finishing my undergraduate degree, I'll go to graduate school.

examples.ko: 학부생이라서 아직 연구실에 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: I'm an undergraduate, so I can't join a research lab yet.

examples.ko: 이 대학교는 학부마다 건물이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: At this university, each college has its own building.
My younger sibling enters the undergraduate program this year.

explain: 한국 대학에서 '학부'는 대학교 4년 과정을 말하고, 그 위 과정은 '대학원'이에요. '경영학부'처럼 학과보다 큰 단위의 이름에도 써요. 학부에 다니는 학생은 '학부생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In a Korean university, '학부' is the undergraduate program, and the level above it is '대학원' (graduate school). It's also used in names of divisions larger than a department, like '경영학부'. A student in it is a '학부생'.

examples.en: He works as a mate on a large ship.

examples.ko: 항해사는 배가 가는 길을 정하고 지도를 봐요.
examples.en: A ship's navigator decides the route and reads the charts.
My father sailed the seas as a ship's officer for twenty years.

examples.ko: 항해사가 되려면 해양 대학에서 공부해야 해요.
examples.en: To become a ship's officer, you have to study at a maritime university.

examples.ko: 선장과 항해사가 날씨를 보고 이야기하고 있어요.
examples.en: The captain and the mate are talking while looking at the weather.

examples.ko: 신입 항해사에게 배 운항 방법을 가르쳐 줬어요.
examples.en: They taught the new mate how to operate the ship.

explain: 선장을 도와 배가 갈 길을 정하고 배를 모는 일을 맡은 선원이에요. 배 전체를 책임지는 사람은 '선장'이고, 엔진을 맡는 사람은 '기관사'라고 해요.
explain_en: This is the crew member who helps the captain plan the route and steer the ship. The person responsible for the whole ship is the '선장' (captain), and the one in charge of the engines is the '기관사' (engineer).

examples.ko: 그 선수는 마흔 살인데도 아직 현역이에요.
examples.en: That player is forty but still active.
My father went to the army on active duty.

examples.ko: 현역 의원들이 오늘 모여서 회의를 했어요.
examples.en: The sitting lawmakers met today for a meeting.

examples.ko: 은퇴한 가수가 현역 시절 노래를 다시 불렀어요.
examples.en: The retired singer sang a song from the days of his career again.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 현역에서 물러나 지금은 감독을 해요.
examples.en: My uncle retired from active play and now works as a coach.

examples.ko: 저 배우는 지금도 현역으로 활동하고 있어요.
examples.en: That actor is still working actively today.

explain: 현역은 지금도 그 일을 하고 있는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '은퇴'예요. 군대에서는 '현역'과 '예비역'을 나눠서 말해요.
explain_en: 현역 is used for someone who is still working in a field, in sports, politics or the military. The opposite is 은퇴 (retirement). In the army, 현역 (active) is separate from 예비역 (reserves).

examples.en: My successor starts work next week.
The team leader has not found a replacement yet.
I taught my successor the job step by step.
I heard the successor is someone with a lot of experience.

examples.ko: 퇴사하기 전에 후임자와 함께 일을 정리했어요.
examples.en: Before leaving the company, I sorted out the work together with my successor.

examples.ko: 후임자로 뽑힌 사람은 저와 같은 학교 출신이에요.
examples.en: The person chosen as my successor graduated from the same school as me.

explain: 회사에서 내 일을 이어받는 사람은 '후임자', 앞서 맡았던 사람은 '전임자'예요. 보통 '후임자를 구하다', '후임자로 정해지다'처럼 써요. 군대에서는 나보다 늦게 들어온 사람을 줄여서 '후임'이라고 많이 불러요.
explain_en: The person who takes over your work is the 후임자, and the one who held the post before is the 전임자. It is used as '후임자를 구하다' (find a successor) or '후임자로 정해지다' (be chosen as successor). In the military, someone who joined after you is often called simply '후임'.
